No two of the four EP-1 verdicts share a full (http_status, body.status, body.upstream) tuple. B_IC_1_CLOSURE.must_not_collide_proof: Four EP-1 verdict forms exist after this correction: AS-1/AS-2 (200, ok, REACHABLE, authenticated:false), AS-3 (503, degraded, UNREACHABLE, authenticated:false), UNKNOWN (200, unknown, UNKNOWN, authenticated:false), and the authenticated form (200, ok, undefined-upstream-field-or-omitted, authenticated:true). Pairwise: AS-1/AS-2 vs AS-3 differ by HTTP status; AS-1/AS-2 vs UNKNOWN differ by body.status and body.upstream while sharing HTTP status; AS-3 vs UNKNOWN differ by HTTP status, body.status and body.upstream; the authenticated form differs from all three unauthenticated forms by body.authenticated. No collision exists.

UNKNOWN_PRODUCERS.rule: Reconciles TA-03's original phrasing, TA-05's budget contract, and the A2 matrix into ONE canonical, exhaustive producer set.
UNKNOWN_PRODUCERS.the_conflict_the_IC_named: v1.0.0 TA-03.contract[0] said UNKNOWN is 'a first-class value for budget exhausted or not yet probed'. TA-04/TA-05 both specify a SYNCHRONOUS, AWAITED, single-flight-coalesced probe on every cache miss - meaning a cache miss never returns without first attempting (and awaiting) a probe. Under that design 'not yet probed' cannot occur as a PERSISTENT, externally observable state for a completed EP-1 response: by the time EP-1 responds, either a probe was attempted and produced a definitive REACHABLE/UNREACHABLE result, or it was never attempted because the budget was already exhausted, or an already-in-flight probe (from a concurrent caller) had not yet settled when this caller's own request needed to respond. v1.0.0 named the first and second cases but not the third, and used language ('not yet probed') that could be misread as a bare, unbounded pending state.

canonical_producer_set.definition: A cache miss or expiry requires a fresh probe, and TA-05's independent request budget has zero remaining tokens this window. No probe is attempted for this request.

A probe for the current cache key is already in flight (TA-04's single-flight coalescing) when this request arrives, and this caller's bounded wait for that in-flight probe's settlement (PROBE_WAIT_BUDGET_MS, a new named constant) elapses before the probe resolves either way. The caller does NOT block indefinitely on a slow or hanging upstream.
canonical_producer_set.why_this_replaces_bare_not_yet_probed: This is the ONLY way 'no valid observation obtained' can occur externally under the synchronous single-flight design, and it IS genuinely observable (a slow or hanging upstream produces it). It is NOT a claim that observation simply has not started yet; it is a claim that a bounded wait for an observation already in progress ran out.

explicitly_excluded_from_UNKNOWN: Genuine upstream unreachability (transport failure, connection refused, DNS failure) - this is AS-3 UNREACHABLE, never UNKNOWN.
A provider 5xx response - this is AS-3 UNREACHABLE, never UNKNOWN.

Any exception the touch's OWN probe logic raises that is not itself a classified transport/provider failure - this MUST fail closed to UNREACHABLE (AS-3), not UNKNOWN. UNKNOWN is reserved exclusively for the two BUDGET/WAIT-based non-observation producers above; it is never a catch-all for an unclassified internal error.
UNKNOWN_PRODUCERS.cold_start_correction: 'Not yet probed' as a bare, persistent, externally observable state is RETRACTED as a producer. It cannot actually occur under TA-04's synchronous-probe-on-miss design, and the mission's own instruction - 'do not claim not yet probed as a persistent externally observable state unless it can actually occur' - is satisfied by this retraction, not by asserting the opposite.

new_technical_parameter.name: PROBE_WAIT_BUDGET_MS
new_technical_parameter.purpose: Bounds how long a caller waits on an ALREADY in-flight probe before answering UNKNOWN via IN_FLIGHT_WAIT_EXCEEDED, rather than hanging the EP-1 response indefinitely on a slow upstream.
new_technical_parameter.rationale: Short enough that EP-1 itself stays a fast liveness check even when the provider is slow; long enough that an ordinary, healthy round trip (well under a second in the normal case) is never mistaken for UNKNOWN. Independently tunable within this range without a new owner act, exactly as TTL_MS and the budget parameters below.

technical_derived_parameters.name: TTL_MS
technical_derived_parameters.rationale: Satisfies the rider's 'short TTL/cache' language (docs/ops/owner-ratifications/M11_HEALTH_CONTRACT_OWNER_DECISIONS_v1.0.0.json ratifications[OD-1].owner_selected_decision.owner_approved_implementation_rider.constraints[0]) without the owner having separately fixed a numeral. Tuning within the admissible range does NOT require a new owner act, because the range is bounded to remain 'short' by construction: the upper bound (60s) keeps bounded staleness within a caller-perceptible window, and the lower bound (5s) keeps the cache meaningfully reducing upstream call volume rather than degenerating to effectively no caching.

B_IC_2_CLOSURE.no_future_owner_act_required_to_tune_TTL: Explicitly: changing TTL_MS to any value within [5000, 60000] ms, while it continues to satisfy the ratified short-TTL/bounded-budget contract, is a technical implementation choice and does NOT require a new owner ratification or a new OC-2-style clarification. PROVIDER_REQUEST_BUDGET_CONTRACT.supersedes: DAG_NODES.nodes[id=TA-05].contract and .done_when in v1.0.0, EXTENDED with concrete magnitude/unit/refill semantics. TA-05's existing constraints (independent of OD-4/KV, fail-closed-to-UNKNOWN) are UNCHANGED and restated here.

BUDGET_MAX_PROBES_PER_WINDOW.lower_bound_invariant: MUST be >= ceil(BUDGET_WINDOW_MS / TTL_MS) at whatever values are actually configured, so a full recovery cycle can always obtain at least one fresh probe within a window even in the worst case where every prior probe in the window failed and was never cached as a success. At the defaults (60000/15000) this invariant requires >= 4; 10 is chosen for margin, not as the tight minimum.

parameters.refill_semantics: FIXED_WINDOW_RESET. The consumed-probe counter resets to zero at each BUDGET_WINDOW_MS boundary. Chosen over a sliding window for testability with fake timers and because the rider's own concern (bounding upstream call volume) does not require sliding-window smoothing.

PROVIDER_REQUEST_BUDGET_CONTRACT.independence_from_OD4_restated: Unchanged from v1.0.0: MUST NOT be implemented on top of proxy.ts's limiter, MUST NOT read KV_REST_API_URL or KV_REST_API_TOKEN.
PROVIDER_REQUEST_BUDGET_CONTRACT.per_instance_restated: Unchanged: PER-INSTANCE. No shared/global budget substrate is authorized by this DAG or this amendment.
PROVIDER_REQUEST_BUDGET_CONTRACT.avoids_permanent_UNKNOWN_after_one_exhau: FIXED_WINDOW_RESET guarantees the budget is never permanently zero: at most BUDGET_WINDOW_MS after exhaustion, the counter resets and a fresh probe becomes possible again. Combined with the lower-bound invariant above, a provider that recovers is always re-observable within one window, never permanently stuck reporting UNKNOWN or stale REACHABLE.
PROVIDER_REQUEST_BUDGET_CONTRACT.testability: Both BUDGET_WINDOW_MS and BUDGET_MAX_PROBES_PER_WINDOW are exported named constants; fake-timer controls advance past a window boundary and assert the counter resets, exactly as TA-04's TTL controls already do for TTL_MS.
PROVIDER_REQUEST_BUDGET_CONTRACT.not_elevated_to_an_owner_decision: Explicitly: these two parameters and their admissible ranges are TECHNICAL. No owner act named or implied them; none is required to adopt or later tune them within their stated ranges.

TEST_EGRESS_CORRECTION.the_gap_the_IC_named: v1.0.0's TA-19 named the problem (the vitest network guard covers only three Gemini/Vertex hostnames) and required a fix, but left 'extend the guard, or inject the transport' as an unresolved either/or, did not enumerate every test file that would need the fix in place before it could safely run, and did not add the edges expressing that ordering to DAG_EDGES.

corrected_TA19_design.mechanism: EXTEND vitest.setup.network-guard.ts's existing transport guard, adding Supabase Auth host coverage alongside the existing BLOCKED_GEMINI_HOSTNAMES set, rather than relying on transport injection alone.
corrected_TA19_design.why_extend_the_harness_guard_rather_than: Three separate test files (TA-13, TA-16, TA-17) exercise code paths that reach the touch, directly or through EP-1. Proving injection covers all three separately is three separate proofs with three chances to miss one; a single harness-level guard covers all three by construction, the same property that already makes the existing Gemini guard effective for every current and future Vitest file rather than only the ones that remember to inject a mock. Per-module injection remains REQUIRED for unit isolation (TA-03's contract already requires the probe target/transport be injectable) but is a UNIT-TESTING property, not a SAFETY property; the harness guard is the safety property.
corrected_TA19_design.host_coverage_measured_precisely: lib/supabase/project-coherence.ts:154 reads `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` as the source of the Auth project's URL (`readInlinedAuthUrl`), which lib/supabase/server.ts's createClient and lib/supabase/proxy.ts's updateSession both pass to createServerClient as the authUrl. There is no single fixed public hostname the way generativelanguage.googleapis.com is fixed for Gemini - the host is per-project (`<ref>.supabase.co`). The guard is therefore extended by SUFFIX PATTERN (hostname ends with '.supabase.co'), which covers the configured project's Auth host regardless of which ref is deployed, PLUS the exact host parsed from `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` if set and not itself localhost, as a second independent check that does not depend on the domain convention holding forever.
corrected_TA19_design.localhost_exclusion_preserved: Unchanged from the existing guard's own stated rationale: the suite legitimately talks to localhost (Supabase, Postgres) and this correction does not touch that exclusion.
corrected_TA19_design.no_opt_out_preserved: No ALLOW_REAL_* escape hatch is introduced by this correction, exactly as v1.0.0 required.
corrected_TA19_design.alternative_not_foreclosed: A future implementer MAY instead prove full transport-injection coverage of TA-13, TA-16 AND TA-17 as an equivalent, but must demonstrate the equivalence with a control per consumer; the harness-guard extension is the default this amendment specifies precisely so that proof is not required per-file.
